raw_response:
I've been farming this land in Quzhou for over fifty years. My knees ache in the cold now, and my son drives the tractor when there's deep ploughing to do. But I still know this soil better than anyone. I'm not going to try something new at my age — wheat and corn, same as always. That's what this land does, that's what the market buys, that's what I know.

My contracted land is about 8 mu. I split it evenly — 4 mu wheat, 4 mu corn on the same plots after harvest. The wheat is already in the ground from last October. Right now it's jointing, so I need to get out with the nitrogen soon. I'll do the topdressing this week before the rain comes, if it comes. For irrigation I go four times on wheat — I did the winter watering already, so jointing, heading, and maybe one more at grain fill. For corn in summer I usually only need two waterings unless it's a dry year.

I buy seeds from the village supply cooperative. I don't experiment — I use the 济麦 variety for wheat that my neighbor also uses, and郑单958 hybrid corn. The agrochemical station told me to cut fertilizer but I apply what my father taught me plus a bit more. Can't risk a bad yield.

Tillage I do rotary before wheat planting. For corn I go no-till now — my son convinced me and it saves money on diesel.
